title: keyboard-shortcuts-discovery-ux-and-screenreader-flow-notes
content:
Purpose and context:

This doc captures UX notes, wireframe write-ups, and a proposed backlog for keyboard shortcut discovery and screen reader flows in the Redwood Console. It is intentionally focused on how keyboard-first users and screen reader users discover, learn, and customize shortcuts. The goal is to outline minimal, testable interactions and accessibility acceptance criteria for Prime features (navigation, search, run/stop inference, open run panel, focus trap cases).

Background / problem statement:
- We ship a growing set of keyboard shortcuts (global nav, run controls, quick search, toggles) but currently lack consistent discovery mechanisms; users either find keyboard hints buried in modal footers or never learn them.
- Screen reader users often cannot infer shortcut availability from the DOM; many shortcut affordances are purely visual (tooltips) and not asserted via ARIA or live regions.
- Conflicts with browser/OS shortcuts (Cmd/Ctrl+K, /, ? etc.) are a source of friction; we need a clear policy and fallback behavior.

Primary user scenarios to cover:
1) New keyboard-first user: lands on Console, wants to know if there are shortcuts and how to see them.
2) Power user: needs a persistent, quick cheat sheet and a way to remap or opt-out of app-level shortcuts.
3) Screen reader user: needs programmatic announcements of shortcut availability on context change and an accessible path to the cheat sheet.
4) Low-vision user: relies on visible high-contrast hints and an easy-to-locate anchor to open the shortcut panel.

Design constraints and principles:
- Progressive disclosure: do not overwhelm first-time users; provide lightweight discovery (one-line hint + link to cheat sheet) and an optional persistent modal for power users.
- Non-intrusive: discovery UI must never intercept typed data or disrupt focus during forms/editor use.
- Accessibility-first: every visible hint must have an accessible equivalent (aria-describedby or aria-live) and the cheat sheet must be fully navigable by keyboard and SR.
- Customizable: allow users to opt-out of global shortcuts and to remap a small safe subset (local storage + account-level settings for paid tiers).

Wireframe write-ups (low-fidelity notes):
1) Top-right help affordance (compact)
- Visual: small outlined ? icon placed left of user avatar; hover shows tooltip: "Keyboard shortcuts: ?" (visual only).
- Accessible: button labelled "Keyboard shortcuts" (aria-label). Pressing opens the Shortcut Panel.
- Keyboard: Tab reaches the button; Enter/Space opens panel. Escape closes panel.

2) Inline one-line discovery hint (first visit)
- Visual: subtle inline text in top-of-page banner for first 3 sessions: "Press ? to open keyboard shortcuts" with a link to "Learn more".
- Accessible: on page load, announce via aria-live polite: "Keyboard shortcuts are available. Press question mark to open." Only announced if user has not dismissed.
- Dismissal: a visually-hidden "dismiss" control to set a flag.

3) Shortcut Cheat Sheet panel (modal dialog)
- Structure: modal with header "Keyboard shortcuts"; two columns: Action + Shortcut. Secondary column: Remap / Disable button per row (hidden behind a settings toggle).
- Focus management: focus is trapped inside modal; initial focus on close button. Each row is a tabbable region with a small button to copy or remap.
- Screen reader: role=dialog, aria-modal=true, aria-labelledby pointing to header; provide an introductory paragraph that lists relevant contexts ("Shortcuts in global nav, editor, and runs").
- Live region: when a shortcut is remapped, announce "Shortcut for Run - now Shift+R".

4) Inline context hints on components
- Small, persistent focus-visible indicators (e.g., dot with keyboard glyph) for actions with shortcuts. Each indicator has aria-describedby linking to its shortcut label.
- Avoid duplication for screen reader: hide visual-only tooltips from assistive tech (aria-hidden=true) and instead surface the text via aria-describedby.

Edge cases / conflict handling:
- Reserved keys (Cmd/Ctrl/Alt combos) policy doc: only allow non-conflicting combos by default; for Cmd/Ctrl+K and slash (/) rely on feature flags and platform detection. If browser prevents binding, fall back to an alternate chord (Shift+Alt+K).
- Focus inside text inputs: global shortcut listeners must ignore key events if the focused element is an input, textarea, or contenteditable.
- Multiple keyboards / international layouts: allow users to test remapped shortcut in the remap UI; show the current key label using KeyboardEvent.key where possible and fall back to code if inconsistent.

Accessibility testing checklist (acceptance criteria):
- Shortcut discovery announcement: on first eligible page load, aria-live announced message is triggered and recorded in test.
- Cheat sheet modal: NVDA/VoiceOver can open, tab through rows, activate remap, and close via Escape; focus returns to invoking control.
- Live region updates: remap and disable actions produce an aria-live assertive update describing the change.
- Focus trap: when modal is open, focus does not escape to background.
- Visual hints: focus-visible styles are present and tested using keyboard-only navigation; high-contrast mode picks up the same styles.
- Input capture: typing in editors and code blocks does not trigger global shortcuts; synthetic tests confirm prevention.

Suggested microcopy (for wireframes and dev):
- Inline hint (polite): "Keyboard shortcuts available — press ? to open."
- Cheat sheet header: "Keyboard shortcuts"; intro paragraph: "Use these shortcuts to move faster in the Console. You can remap or disable shortcuts in Settings."
- Remap confirmation: "Shortcut updated: {Action} is now {KeyCombo}."
- Conflict warning: "{KeyCombo} conflicts with your browser or OS. Choose a different shortcut or disable app shortcuts."
- Opt-out CTA in settings: "Disable app keyboard shortcuts" with description "Prevents the app from intercepting keyboard combinations."

Proposed backlog tickets (short-form items for grooming):
- CON-1023: Add keyboard discovery aria-live announcement on first session; flag persisted in localStorage.
- CON-1024: Implement compact "Keyboard shortcuts" help button in header; accessibility label and keyboard focus.
- CON-1025: Create Shortcut Cheat Sheet modal component (design + interactions + remap baseline).
- CON-1026: Implement per-action aria-describedby pointers and visual hint component.
- CON-1027: Remap UI MVP (local remap only, persisted to account for logged-in users).
- CON-1028: Conflict detection service (client-side heuristics + telemetry) to surface suggestion when browser prevents binding.
- CON-1029: E2E tests for shortcut modal and live region announcements (Playwright + VoiceOver smoke).
- CON-1030: Settings toggle to disable app shortcuts and opt-out policy doc.

Acceptance criteria (example for CON-1025):
- Modal opens with keyboard and screen reader.
- Focus trapped inside modal and returns to opener on close.
- Remap flow renders and updates live region message.
- All rows are reachable by keyboard and have logical tab order.
- Visual and accessible labels match the microcopy guidelines above.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should remaps be account-wide or device-local for the initial MVP? (Recommendation: device-local first; account sync for Enterprise.)
- Do we allow chords that include Alt/Option on macOS where the OS may interfere? (Recommendation: allow but warn.)
- How do we handle localization for key names (e.g., AZERTY vs QWERTY)? (Recommendation: show both label and raw code on hover in remap UI.)

Implementation notes for engineering:
- Use a shared ShortcutRegistry module (singleton) that exposes: register(actionId, defaultKeyCombo, scope), unregister(actionId), getActiveBindings(), remap(actionId, newCombo). Hook into global keydown with a short-circuit for inputs/contenteditable.
- For a11y: prefer aria-describedby over visible tooltips for screen reader text. Use aria-live polite for non-blocking announcements and assertive for remap confirmations.
- Store remaps in localStorage key "console.shortcuts.v1" and add a backend sync API for later. Respect privacy & telemetry opt-out.

Next steps / plan for next 2 sprints:
- Sprint A: Design + microcopy, implement help button and discovery aria-live (CON-1023, CON-1024), basic cheat sheet modal skeleton (no remap).
- Sprint B: Remap MVP (CON-1027), per-action hint markers (CON-1026), conflict detection telemetry (CON-1028). Create Playwright tests for visits and announcements (CON-1029).

Notes to reviewers:
- Pay attention to remap scope: local vs account; this has UX implications for multi-device users.
- Validation needed on keyboard glyphs for i18n: are we comfortable with showing user-facing key labels that differ by layout?

References / prior art:
- Gmail "Keyboard shortcuts" cheat sheet (pattern)
- VS Code Quick Open / Command Palette (remap patterns)
- W3C WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: modal dialogs and live regions

Draft attachments to create in next iteration:
- Low-fidelity wireframe: cheat-sheet-modal.png (annotated)
- Interaction flow: shortcut-remap-sequence.sketch
- Playwright test plan: shortcut-modal-playwright.md

End of doc.
